text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today after climbing to a two-week high of $142.28 on November 13th. The pullback comes as crude oil prices have retreated slightly—US oil is trading at $89.62 per barrel, down from the levels that likely supported last week's run-up. The stock is now down 4.3% over two weeks, suggesting some profit-taking after the recent rally.

The broader context is mixed: while heating oil prices remain sharply elevated (up 59% year-over-year), which typically supports energy company margins, there's no major company-specific catalyst in the recent news to drive the stock higher. The modest decline appears to be a reversion toward recent average levels rather than a reaction to new negative information.
